steps: Cell specialization is the process by which cells become adapted in their structure and function to perform particular jobs.
Specialized cells have features suited to their functions.
For example, red blood cells carry oxygen, nerve cells transmit messages, and muscle cells contract to produce movement.
In multicellular organisms, specialized cells work together to perform the functions of the organism.
items.finalAnswer: Cell specialization adapts cells to particular functions; examples include red blood cells, nerve cells and muscle cells.

steps: The nucleus controls the activities of the cell and contains the instructions for making proteins.
Ribosomes use these instructions to synthesize proteins.
If coordination between the nucleus and ribosomes fails, protein synthesis may be disturbed or stop.
Without the proteins needed for its activities, the cell may malfunction and may eventually die.
This coordination is important because proteins are needed for the structure and proper functioning of the cell.
items.finalAnswer: If coordination fails, the cell may not make the proteins it needs, causing it to malfunction or die.
